title: Non-blocking finding from PR #419's review (frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups)
description: pr-reviewer accepted PR #419 (closing the type-checking gap for frontend/eslint-rules/no-restricted-src-import.test.ts by adding eslint-rules to tsconfig.node.json's include and allowJs). While independently re-verifying the PR's `as unknown as Linter.Config[]` cast (the task's own decisions entry: '...so a single explicit cast ... is more honest than fighting the mismatch property-by-property' and the in-file comment claiming 'nothing short of a cast bridges them'), pr-reviewer found that a direct, single-hop `as Linter.Config[]` cast (without the `unknown` detour) also compiles cleanly against the real `eslintConfigDefault` import -- verified empirically by swapping the cast in place and running a from-scratch `yarn tsc -b --noEmit --force` (clean, no errors). The two packages' flat-config types genuinely are NOT mutually assignable via a plain `return`/assignment (confirmed separately: `Partial<Record<string, Processor>>` is not assignable to `Record<string, Processor> | undefined` due to index-signature strictness -- TS2322), but TypeScript's looser 'comparability' rule for a bare `as` type assertion (as opposed to assignment) does accept the cast directly, without needing to round-trip through `unknown` first. This matters because `as unknown as T` fully defeats comparability checking for any value regardless of its actual type (confirmed: casting an unrelated `number` to `Linter.Config[]` via `as unknown as` raises no error, while a bare `as Linter.Config[]` on that same `number` correctly fails with TS2352 'neither type sufficiently overlaps'), so the direct form is strictly safer for no loss of capability here and would still catch a future accidental import-shape drift that the current double-hop cast would silently swallow. Non-blocking: the current code is correct, the wiring test's assertions are unaffected by the choice of cast (casts are compile-time only), and the mismatch is otherwise thoroughly documented inline.

checklist.step: Replace `eslintConfigDefault as unknown as Linter.Config[]` in frontend/eslint-rules/no-restricted-src-import.test.ts with the direct, single-hop `eslintConfigDefault as Linter.Config[]` (no `unknown` detour), and update the inline comment above it (and, since it's referenced there too, the parent task's decisions-entry language if a fresh decisions entry is added) so the claim is 'a cast, but not necessarily through unknown' rather than implying the double-hop is required. Re-run `yarn tsc -b --noEmit --force` to confirm it stays clean with the narrower cast, and `yarn vitest run eslint-rules` to confirm the wiring suite's behavior is unaffected (casts are erased at compile time, so this is expected to be a no-op at runtime).

docs/architecture/Testing.md (around the paragraph describing this fix) claims 'every real type annotation in the test file now is[checked]... against the real exported types of both modules'. This overstates what's actually checked for the wiring-test block specifically: `eslintConfig` (used by `eslintConfig.find(...)`, `.plugins`, `.rules` in the 'wiring' describe block) is checked against `eslint`'s own `Linter.Config` shape -- the cast target -- not against `eslint.config.js`'s actual declared return type (`typescript-eslint`'s `TSESLint.FlatConfig.Config[]`/`ConfigWithExtends[]` from `tseslint.config(...)`), precisely because the cast at the import boundary substitutes one type for the other. If `eslint.config.js`'s exported shape ever drifted in a way incompatible with `Linter.Config` but still a valid flat config, tsc would not catch it for that half of the file, contradicting the doc's 'real exported types of both modules' framing for that portion. (The `isBlockedSrcSource`-table block, which has no cast involved, is checked against the real exported type and is unaffected by this -- the imprecision is specific to the post-cast wiring-test code.) Independently flagged by a concurrently-running code-review pass during PR #419's review. Reword Testing.md's claim to be accurate about the cast boundary, or scope the claim to the parts of the file it actually covers.

decisions.decision: For item 2, reworded docs/architecture/Testing.md's claim by splitting it into two cases instead of just narrowing scope: the isBlockedSrcSource-table block is checked against no-restricted-src-import.js's real exported type directly (unaffected, kept the existing TS2345 proof), while the wiring-test block is checked against the cast's target type (Linter.Config) rather than eslint.config.js's own declared return type, and spelled out the resulting gap (an eslint.config.js shape drift that stays flat-config-valid but diverges from Linter.Config would not be caught here).
decisions.rationale: The task description itself distinguishes the two blocks (isBlockedSrcSource-table vs. wiring-test), so keeping that split in the doc keeps the paragraph's useful information intact rather than just softening the overstated claim into vague language. Considered only trimming the 'real exported types of both modules' phrase to 'a real exported type' without explaining why the wiring-test block differs, but that would lose the precise mechanism (cast-at-import-boundary swaps the checked type) that makes the original claim inaccurate in the first place.

review.notes: Independently re-verified both closed findings. (1) Cast narrowing: reproduced the TS2352 proof (added `const __probe = 42 as Linter.Config[]`, got TS2352; the old `as unknown as` form would not have caught it), confirmed `yarn tsc -b --noEmit --force` clean, and mutation-tested the wiring suite by commenting out the rule's registration in the real eslint.config.js (4/21 failures as expected, confirming the narrower cast isn't masking a detection gap), then restored it (21/21 clean). (2) Testing.md reword: read the full paragraph, verified the TSESLint.FlatConfig.ConfigArray = Config[] claim against @typescript-eslint/utils's own .d.ts, and judged the rewrite precisely accurate (not merely softened) -- it correctly distinguishes the isBlockedSrcSource-table block (checked against the real type) from the wiring-test block (checked against the cast's target, Linter.Config, not eslint.config.js's own declared return type) and spells out the residual gap. (3) Parent task's appended decisions entry: read the full array -- the two pre-existing entries are untouched, the new third entry is purely appended (append-only convention honored), and its characterization of what the original entry did/didn't claim is accurate. (4) make e2e skip is correct: diff touches only Testing.md, 3 task-board JSON files, and one test-file cast/comment -- no application code, no UI surface. Full matrix re-run independently: backend pytest 1655 passed/99.95% coverage, ruff/mypy clean; frontend yarn lint clean, tsc -b --noEmit --force clean, vitest run --coverage 105 files/1104 tests passed (99.78-99.84%); scripts/validate_tasks.py 399 files clean; CLAUDE.md/.claude confirmed untouched via diff. A backgrounded code-review pass (medium effort) over the same diff independently returned zero findings. area/skill mean verify-elder-signal and architecture-review don't apply; no frontend component touched so the common/-vs-feature placement check doesn't apply; no API route/schema touched so no OpenAPI concern. No blocking findings, and no new non-blocking findings -- this chain has converged; no further follow-up task filed, as instructed.
